morning.insight:
💡 오늘 회의의 주제와 시장의 질문이 같습니다

2027 전사전략회의를 여는 날, 글로벌 시장은 'AI에 얼마를 썼고 무엇을 증명했나'를 심판하고 있습니다. 알파벳·인텔·아마존·메타가 실적 하나로 시총을 잃은 건 기술이 틀렸다는 뜻이 아니라, 비용의 크기를 성과의 언어로 번역하지 못했다는 뜻입니다. 오늘 AX 2차 보고와 세부사업계획을 다룰 때도 같은 잣대를 써보세요 — '무엇을 도입했나'가 아니라 '무엇이 얼마나 줄었나'.

국내 증시는 외국인이 3,731억 팔아도 기관이 1조2,329억 받아내며 +2.24% 올랐습니다. 수급의 방향이 아니라 받아내는 힘이 지수를 만들었다는 것. 원화는 1,343원대로 밀리고 있어 수입 물가·연수 비용은 계속 눈여겨봐야 합니다.

밀린 항목 15건 중 절반이 '10월 마감'입니다. 오늘 다 하려 하지 마시고, Z-P2와 Z-P3 두 개만 확실히 가져가시면 충분한 하루입니다. 좋은 회의 되십시오, 형!

articles.headline: 유가 100달러 아래…수입 물가 부담 완화 기대
articles.eng: Oil below $100 eases import-price pressure
articles.body: 미·이란 카타르 채널 외교 접촉으로 WTI가 95달러대로 8% 급락하며 브렌트유도 100달러 아래로 내려왔다. 국내 수입 물가와 원가 부담이 완화될 것이라는 기대가 커졌다.

articles.headline: 이재명 대통령 시정연설…확장재정 기조 '821조 예산'
articles.eng: President Lee outlines expansionary 821tn won budget
articles.body: 이재명 대통령이 시정연설에서 '재정의 적극적 역할'을 강조하며 2027년도 예산안 심의 협조를 요청했다. 확장재정 기조가 내년 예산 심의의 출발점이 될 전망이다.

articles.headline: Election Day Arrives With Control of Congress in the Balance
articles.body: Voters head to the polls with all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats on the line, as both parties make their final pitches on a midterm widely framed as a referendum on the Trump presidency.

articles.headline: How the Midterms Could Move Markets
articles.body: Investors are weighing how a potential shift in control of Congress could reshape regulation, taxes and tariffs, with markets steadying after oil's sharp drop eased some inflation fears.

articles.headline: The 'What If' Midterms: What Polls Say — and Why They Could Be Wrong
articles.body: Pollsters are largely selling a Democratic advantage heading into the Nov. 3 vote, but in the Trump era the polls have often been wrong — leaving open a 'what if' scenario on both sides.

articles.headline: Your Guide to 2026 Midterm Election Night
articles.body: From the first poll closures in South Carolina to the late tallies, here is a state-by-state guide to what to watch Tuesday night and which races will decide control of the Senate and House.

articles.headline: Oil Plunges 7% as US-Iran Diplomatic Channel Opens
articles.body: Crude oil tumbled about 7% after the US and Iran made diplomatic contact through Qatar, easing fears over the Strait of Hormuz and pulling WTI toward the $95-a-barrel level.

articles.headline: Tech Stocks Slump for a Third Session as AI Spending Doubts Persist
articles.body: The Nasdaq fell for a third straight session as doubts over the payoff from massive AI investment weighed on megacaps, while the Dow rose on a rotation into value and traditional stocks.

articles.headline: US Tech Stocks Hover Near Correction on Middle East and AI Worries
articles.body: Technology stocks are leading US equities lower as renewed Middle East tensions and worries over the artificial-intelligence trade keep the sector near correction territory, even as oil's drop offered some relief.

articles.headline: AI Giants Commit to $895 Billion in Spending as Capital Race Intensifies
articles.body: Big technology companies are locking in hundreds of billions of dollars in AI-related capital spending, intensifying an arms race that is increasingly drawing scrutiny over whether the investment will pay off.

articles.headline: Oil Slides as US-Iran Qatar Channel Eases Hormuz Tension
articles.body: Crude prices fell sharply on optimism that US-Iran diplomatic contact through Qatar could ease tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, a key chokepoint for global oil flows.

articles.headline: Anthropic IPO Could Draw Junk Rating, Adding to AI-Sector Concerns
articles.body: Anthropic's public-market debut is raising fresh questions after reports that the AI developer could receive a junk credit rating, compounding worries about the sector's profitability.

articles.headline: Apple, AMD Earnings to Test the AI Rally This Week
articles.body: Earnings from Apple and AMD this week will be a key test for the AI trade after last week's rout, with investors focused on capital-spending guidance as the metric for whether AI is translating into returns.

articles.headline: Gold Tops $3,950 as Haven Demand Rises
articles.body: Gold climbed above $3,950 an ounce as investors sought havens amid election uncertainty and a sharp equity selloff in technology shares.

articles.headline: Early Voting Surge Offers Promising Sign for Democrats on Midterm Eve
articles.body: A surge in early voting is offering a promising sign for Democrats heading into Election Day, with interviews revealing voters focused on affordability, health care and the economy.

articles.headline: Parties End the Midterm Election With Their Closing Arguments
articles.body: The tumultuous midterm campaign barreled into its final full day, with both parties delivering closing arguments in a contest widely seen as a referendum on the Trump presidency.

articles.headline: Our Final Polls: Democrats Show Strength in Senate Battlegrounds
articles.body: Democrats are ahead of Republicans in nearly all seven battleground states that will determine control of the Senate, according to the final Times/Siena polls of the cycle.

articles.headline: How AI Spending Doubts Are Rewriting the Tech Trade
articles.body: After earnings shocks at Alphabet, Intel and Amazon, investors are demanding that AI investment be proven through results rather than promises, reshaping the technology trade.

articles.headline: Oil's Sharp Drop Eases Inflation Fears Ahead of the Vote
articles.body: A sharp drop in oil prices on renewed US-Iran diplomacy is easing inflation fears just as voters head to the polls, offering some relief to a campaign dominated by affordability concerns.

articles.headline: Trump's Popularity at All-Time Lows as Referendum on Presidency
articles.body: Like most midterms, this election appears to be largely a referendum on the president, and Trump's approval rating sits at all-time lows heading into the final stretch.

articles.headline: Election 2026: Trump's Final Rally and Texas Candidates' Last Push
articles.body: Candidates made their final pitches on the eve of the midterms, with Ken Paxton making his last stand in Texas as both parties sprinted to the finish line of a high-stakes campaign.

articles.headline: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Set Aside 20,000 California Ballots
articles.body: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots for now, the latest legal skirmish over voting rules on the eve of the midterm election.

articles.headline: The House Races That Should Raise Alarms Among Republicans
articles.body: A guide to the competitive House districts that could decide control of the chamber, with several Republican-held seats emerging as early indicators of a potential Democratic wave.

articles.headline: Trump Faces a Future Without the Rallies That Made Him a Political Force
articles.body: As Election Day approached, Trump appeared to contemplate the end of an era, telling supporters at his final rally that he was 'closing it down' — a turning point for the rallies that defined his political career.

articles.headline: Hegseth Just Showed Again Why He Needs to Go
articles.body: Columnist Max Boot argues that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's latest controversy is another reminder of why he should be impeached or removed from office.

articles.headline: Oil Prices Fall as US-Iran Diplomacy Eases Supply Fears
articles.body: Oil prices tumbled on reports of diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran, easing supply fears that had pushed crude sharply higher in recent weeks.

articles.headline: US Tech Stocks Tumble as Concerns Over AI Spending Intensify
articles.body: US technology stocks extended their slide as concerns intensified over whether the industry's massive AI spending will deliver adequate returns, deepening a selloff that has rattled markets.

articles.headline: Meta Rekindles AI Spending Fears as Market Value Sinks $124bn
articles.body: Meta's market value sank by $124 billion after the social media group said it would raise 'hundreds of billions of dollars' in coming years, rekindling fears over runaway AI spending.

articles.headline: Nasdaq Tumbles While Treasuries Soar as AI Fears Mount
articles.body: The Nasdaq tumbled while Treasuries rallied as investors sought safety, with mounting worries about AI spending and high oil prices weighing on risk appetite.

articles.headline: Oil Falls Sharply on US-Iran Diplomatic Breakthrough
articles.body: Crude prices dropped sharply on progress in US-Iran talks over the Strait of Hormuz, easing fears that had threatened global oil flows through the key waterway.

articles.headline: Anthropic Could Receive Junk Rating After IPO
articles.body: Anthropic could receive a junk credit rating after its public listing, revelations that add to concerns over the AI industry's financial health and profitability.

articles.headline: US Midterms: Democrats Eye House Control as Polls Close
articles.body: Democrats head into the November 3 midterms with a solid generic-ballot lead, raising the prospect of a blue wave that could hand them control of the House.
